svg.title: Inference Traffic Flow — Private AI Code Assistant
svg.desc: Deployment view of the Private AI Code Assistant. A single OpenAI-compatible HTTPS connection links Dev Spaces assistants to MaaS / RHCL with API-key authentication. The main arrows show chat passing through input guardrails and Semantic Router, which is step 4 below guardrails. One bottom connection from Semantic Router splits into a solid local route to step 5 and a dashed optional route to external model APIs outside the cluster on the left. Step 5 combines the llm-d gateway and EPP-integrated Envoy proxy; Envoy routes each request to the selected vLLM replica in step 6. Two illustrative replica pods each contain an NVIDIA GPU tile and PVC storage strip. This scale-out topology and EPP route require custom configuration; the supplied chart creates one replica mounting the model-cache PVC. The right column contains Key Architecture Properties, OpenShift AI Capabilities, and Observability, in that order. The capabilities panel shows only KServe model serving, Models as a Service, TrustyAI guardrails, and GPU hardware profiles used by this project, without any arrows attached to that panel. Continue autocomplete bypass behavior is noted in the properties panel. Observability records GPU, latency, token, cache, gateway, and guardrail metrics through ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor scrapes into Prometheus time series; Grafana queries them through Thanos. vLLM middleware sends per-request message histories, response content, and token usage to Langfuse through its HTTP/JSON ingestion API. vLLM exports inference timing and spans over OTLP/gRPC to OTel Collector, which forwards them over OTLP/HTTP to Langfuse. The guardrails proxy sends flagged inputs, detector results and scores, and block or warning actions through the Langfuse HTTP/JSON ingestion API. These are per-request records; full agent and tool trajectories are not linked. KServe controls model lifecycle. The bottom request-flow legend and separate Routing Decisions panel are omitted.
